the definition of a security-oriented methodology that allows CSPs to set-up security capabilities and to offer them as-a-service, so that customers can specify and enforce their security requirements through a Security SLAs.

our approach can be seen as a first step towards the definition of a catalogue of security features and capabilities that can be used to define Security SLAs and that can be offered by CSPs as-a-service.

the methodology proposed in this paper allows CSPs to define security capabilities that can then be offered to their customers, and to specify the guarantees associated to the offered capabilities, by using a Security SLA that can be monitored by customers during operation.

the paper presents a methodology to set up a catalogue of security as-a-service capabilities and to specify security SLAs, which are based on the catalogue, in a way that is compliant with both customer and provider requirements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have proposed a methodology for defining a catalogue of security services that can be offered on top of existing cloud services, and a methodology to specify security requirements and to monitor the security capabilities offered by providers.
we propose an approach for the design and implementation of Security SLAs that are automatically verifiable by customers.
we have defined a methodology to set up a catalogue of security features that can serve as a reference for providers willing to define security SLAs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by means of a systematic and well-defined process, providers are able to define and implement the security capabilities they are willing to offer, and customers can assess the security guarantees offered by providers, in a transparent and unambiguous way.
the definition of security capabilities, as well as their enforcement, should be driven by the requirements expressed in the Security SLAs.
the definition of a catalogue of security features to be offered by a cloud service provider can be a fundamental step towards the adoption of security-oriented SLAs.
